messages:
alex_g: Quick check-in from the canary run of the micro-slotting experiment. Observed odd tail behavior for long sequences (256+ tokens). Avg latency nudged down but 99.9th spiked. Dumping what I have below and a couple hypotheses.

maria_p: link to the perf dump? also which config did you run (batch interval / coalesce / jitter / token budget)?

alex_g: perf dump: https://internal.perf/trace/slotting-2345 (internal)
config snippet:
```
batch_interval_ms=4
coalesce_delay_ms=7
jitter_ms=1-10
token_budget_target=2048
slotting_mode=adaptive
```
client load: steady 500 qps with 2x 2s bursts every 30s.

sam_k: saw kernel flip around the same timestamps in the trace. fast_attn -> fallback_kernel when KV-miss-burst > 0.12. That fallback costs ~6-8ms per token in the hot path.

jordana: can you paste the KV hit/miss counters around the spike window? wondering if eviction thrash is lining up with micro-window boundaries.

alex_g: KV window stats (aggregated 1s buckets):
```
kv_hit_rate: 0.88
kv_miss_rate: 0.12
miss_burst_count: 14 (within 120ms window)
cache_evictions/sec: 32
```
miss bursts map to micro-window boundaries +/- jitter.

ci-bot: perf-report uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/234567 (summary CSV + flamegraphs) :white_check_mark:

maria_p: rough hypothesis: increasing jitter amplitude reduced avg queueing but aligned some evictions with coalesce boundaries, creating correlated misses that flip kernels. Two quick levers: lower micro-window to 2ms (less alignment) OR add randomized exponential jitter so evictions smear. Also consider raising token_budget_target for long sequences (3072) so those requests don't get split or hit fallback kernels as often.

sam_k: I ran a small sim with synthetic arrivals: micro-window=2ms, jitter=0-6ms (exp backoff), token_budget=3072. Results on canary (same load): 99.9th dropped from ~420ms -> ~320ms, avg latency ~ -6ms, throughput -4% (due to slightly less coalescing). Kernel flip count dropped by ~60%.

alex_g: awesome. can you share the sim config and the quick script you used to force kernel pin so we can isolate fallback impact?

sam_k: script: 
```
# pin to fast_attn kernel for canary group
./canary_ctl set kernel_preference fast_attn --group micro-slot-canary
# run load generator
./loadgen --qps 500 --burst-pattern "2s@30s" --seq-len 256 --token-budget 3072
```
logs show kernel_pin reduced flips but memory usage +1.8GB on avg.

jordana: FYI incident INC-7892 linked to the earlier SLO chime — two customers hit 99.9th > 500ms during the first experiment rollout. Ops paged, but auto-fallback kept requests alive.

alex_g: thanks — plan: 1) roll micro-window=2ms + jitter exp(0-6ms) + token_budget_target=3072 to canary with kernel pin toggle off by default but available for tests, 2) run overnight extended bursts (2x) and monitor kernel flip count + KV eviction rate, 3) collect flamegraphs and flame timelines. I'll post updates in the morning. :thumbsup:

maria_p: add a tracing hook to tag requests that experienced fallback kernel so we can correlate downstream errors/regressions. Also add a metric for "miss_burst_in_window" (counts bursts >3 misses in 200ms).

alex_g: added to canary config plan. will attach traces tomorrow.

sam_k: if overnight run looks stable, we should try lowering coalesce_delay to 5ms on the next canary to regain some throughput. but only after verifying kernel flip risk is under threshold.

alex_g: agreed. end-of-thread summary: micro-window->2ms, jitter->exp 0-6ms, token_budget->3072, kernel_pin available for debug, monitor KV miss bursts + kernel flips + 99.9th. next update ~tomorrow morning.
